details.description: MiniMax-M2.5 is MiniMax's mixture-of-experts chat model for agentic and office-productivity work, with 229 billion total parameters and 10 billion active per token, an iterative update to the M2/M2.1 family. It was trained largely through reinforcement learning across more than 200,000 real-world environments and is tuned for coding, tool calling and web search, and document work in Word, Excel and PowerPoint. MiniMax released it on February 12, 2026 under a Modified MIT license; a faster 'M2.5-Lightning' variant trades a higher price for higher throughput.
advantages: Scores 76.3% on BrowseComp with context management.
M2.5-Lightning sustains 100 output tokens/second, which MiniMax says is twice the throughput of other frontier models.
disadvantages: Text only; no image or audio input.
Artificial Analysis measured a higher hallucination rate (88%) than the prior M2.1 (67%), alongside only a modest accuracy gain (25% vs. 22%).
use_cases: Agentic coding across languages including Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust and Java.
Office productivity tasks in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, including financial modeling.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.5: Built for Real-World Productivity
MiniMax-M2.5: Everything you need to know

notes: Catalog facts give conflicting max_input_tokens across snapshots (196,000 and 1,000,000) and max_output_tokens (8,000 and 8,192). Artificial Analysis states a 200K-token context window, matching the smaller catalog figure; no source found confirms the 1,000,000 figure, so the description avoids stating a specific context-window number. Total/active parameter counts (229B/10B) are corroborated by both MiniMax's own announcement and Artificial Analysis.
